title: Rigveda 9.33: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.33: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.33 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 680r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.33.1-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 680r
translation.original_text:
1pra somā̍so vipa̱ścito̱ 'pāṁ na ya̍nty ū̱rmaya̍ḥ | vanā̍ni mahi̱ṣā i̍va ||
2a̱bhi droṇā̍ni ba̱bhrava̍ḥ śu̱krā ṛ̱tasya̱ dhāra̍yā | vāja̱ṁ goma̍ntam akṣaran ||
3su̱tā indrā̍ya vā̱yave̱ varu̍ṇāya ma̱rudbhya̍ḥ | somā̍ arṣanti̱ viṣṇa̍ve ||
4ti̱sro vāca̱ ud ī̍rate̱ gāvo̍ mimanti dhe̱nava̍ḥ | hari̍r eti̱ kani̍kradat ||
5a̱bhi brahmī̍r anūṣata ya̱hvīr ṛ̱tasya̍ mā̱tara̍ḥ | ma̱rmṛ̱jyante̍ di̱vaḥ śiśu̍m ||
6rā̱yaḥ sa̍mu̱drām̐ś ca̱turo̱ 'smabhya̍ṁ soma vi̱śvata̍ḥ | ā pa̍vasva saha̱sriṇa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1LIKE waves of waters, skilled in song the juices of the Soma speed Onward, as buffaloes to woods.
2With stream of sacrifice the brown bright drops have flowed with strength in store Of kine into the wooden vats.
3To Indra, Vâyu, Varuṇa, to Vishṇu, and the Maruts, flow The drops of Soma juice effused.
4Three several words are uttered: kine are lowing, cows who give their milk: The Tawny-hued goes bellowing on.
5The young and sacred mothers of the holy rite have uttered praise: They decorate the Child of Heaven.
6From every side, O Soma, for our profit, pour thou forth four seas Filled full of riches thousandfold.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 680r (numbered 102r by the scribe) (OPenn image 680, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.32.5 ‹yathā hitam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 680v (numbered 102v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.34.3 ‹duhanti śakmanā payaḥ›. Verses 9.33.1-6 end on this page.

1pra | somāsaḥ | vipaḥ-citaḥ | apām | na | yanti | ūrmayaḥ | vanāni | mahiṣāḥ-iva
2abhi | droṇāni | babhravaḥ | śukrāḥ | ṛtasya | dhārayā | vājam | go-mantam | akṣaran
3sutāḥ | indrāya | vāyave | varuṇāya | marut-bhyaḥ | somāḥ | arṣanti | viṣṇave
